subject: Clarify: Use of Customer Data for Model Training & Retention
messages:
From: Elena Popov <legal@finova-bank.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finova-bank.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 14:15:00 +0100
Subject: Data use question: training + retention details

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Before our procurement review can proceed we need written responses to a couple of technical/legal points for the security pack: 

1) Does Redwood ever use customer-provided prompts, files, or model outputs to train or fine-tune models (i.e., add to model training corpora or weights updates)?
2) For hosted API customers, what telemetry or logs are retained by Redwood, for how long, and what elements are included (full prompts, metadata, output text, IP headers, etc.)?
3) Are there any exceptions where customer data could be used for research/aggregation/training? If so, how are customers notified and can they opt out?
4) Specific question about the KV cache / prefix cache: is that persisted to disk or sent outside EU regions?

Could you provide a short written summary and any supporting documents (SOC2 exhibits, DPA excerpts, short legal statement) we can include in our security questionnaire? I attached our consolidated list of questions (Finova_Security_Qs.xlsx).

We'd like to get this to our InfoSec review by next Tuesday. If helpful, please loop in your security lead.

Best,
Elena Popov
Head of Legal - Finova Bank
Elena.Popov@finova-bank.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data use question: training + retention details

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front to help your review: for enterprise customers we provide contractual "no-model-training" commitments and regionally scoped retention controls; we do not use customer prompts/outputs to train models when that commitment is in place. Full details below and I've attached a short summary and our SOC2 control list for your security pack.

Attachment: redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf (PDF, 78KB)
Attachment: Finova_SOC2_Control_List.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

Summary details (high level):
- Model training: Redwood's default product behavior depends on the deployment mode.
  - Hosted (self-serve): aggregated telemetry may be used to improve service quality and guardrails; customer content is not directly copied into public training corpora.
  - Hosted (enterprise contract): we can commit contractually that customer content will not be used to train models ("no-model-training" clause) and will be excluded from telemetry used for research.
  - Dedicated / Private: customer data is isolated in customer tenancy; it is not accessible to Redwood research or training processes.
- Telemetry & logs: by default we retain service debug logs (traces, request ids, limited metadata) for 30 days, and audit logs for 90 days; the contents and retention windows are configurable per enterprise contract. Logged request payloads (prompts/outputs) are not included in long-term training stores when the no-training commitment is active.
- KV cache: KV/prefix caches are ephemeral and held in memory on the inference host; for Dedicated/Private deployments they do not leave the customer environment. For Hosted enterprise customers we persist only short-lived debugging traces and never materialize KV cache to long-term storage.
- Exceptions & opt-out: any use of customer content for model improvement is opt-in for enterprise customers; there are no hidden training pipelines.

I'm cc'ing Vivek (security) to confirm the technical controls and Monica (your account lead) to coordinate contract language. Happy to run through this on a 30-min call next week.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — Vivek here (Head of Security & Compliance). Thanks for the detailed questions; below is a concise technical confirmation you can share with InfoSec. I've attached a signed one-page statement for your records.

Attachment: no_training_affidavit.pdf (PDF, 12KB)

Technical confirmation (for Finova Bank):
1) Training and model updates
- Redwood does NOT incorporate customer prompts, uploaded files, or model outputs into any training datasets or weight updates when a contractual "no-model-training" commitment is in place. That includes derived artifacts (embeddings, labeled examples) unless explicitly agreed in writing.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments customer data stays within the customer tenancy and is not accessible to Redwood engineering/research for training.

2) Telemetry vs. customer content
- "Telemetry" for self-serve accounts is limited to aggregated service metrics (latency percentiles, error rates, resource utilization). Textual request/response payloads are not used to build training corpora for our public models.
- For enterprise-hosted accounts we provide options to completely opt out of any textual telemetry retention beyond short-lived debugging traces.

3) KV cache persistence
- KV/prefix caches are memory-resident and ephemeral. They are not serialized to persistent storage by default and are purged after the inference session. For Dedicated/Private deployments, we additionally ensure eviction handlers clear in-memory caches and do not snapshot them to disk.

4) Retention and deletion workflow
- Default enterprise retention policy: debug traces and request payloads are retained for 30 days; audit logs are retained for 90 days. These windows are configurable in the enterprise DPA.
- Deletion procedure: customers may request immediate deletion via the Console or an API call; requests generate an audit ticket and a deletion job with a verifiable job id (e.g., DEL-<ticket>). Deletion jobs are generally completed within 72 hours for covered artifacts; longer windows for archived backups are documented in the DPA.
- Proof of deletion: we provide a signed deletion certificate (job id + timestamp + SHA256 of the removed object manifest) on request for enterprise customers.

5) Exceptions and notifications
- Any use of customer content for research or model improvement is strictly opt-in and requires explicit written customer consent and contract amendment; we will notify customers and provide an opt-out mechanism.

Next steps: Monica, can we send Elena the standard DPA excerpt and a redlined contract clause for the "no-model-training" language and the deletion certificate template? Elena, if you want these as formal exhibits I can get legal to countersign the affidavit and provide the deletion-certificate template today.
